title: Interim funding to keep THEMUSEUM open
subtitle: Council also granted a noise exemption for downtown special events and held a closed session on litigation.
overview: Council held a special meeting mainly to decide whether to give THEMUSEUM up to $300,000 in emergency cash-flow support. The downtown museum told Council its board would meet the following week to consider winding down without help. Council approved the support {{vote:m1}}. Funding is paid in stages through August 15 and only if needed to stay cash-flow positive.

The agreement has conditions. THEMUSEUM must report monthly cash flow and limit discretionary spending. It must honour summer camps and venue rentals. It must start a collaborative review of its business model by June 1. Council also required THEMUSEUM to ask the Region of Waterloo to cover half of the interim cost {{vote:m2}}. An amendment to defer the final payment to June 24 was defeated {{vote:m3}}.

For residents, the decision keeps a major downtown attraction and its summer camps running while a new, sustainable operating model is explored. Council also approved a noise exemption for downtown special events {{vote:m4}}. After the meeting, Council went into closed session on a litigation matter. The minutes report no outcome from it.

decisions.detail: Council authorized an agreement giving THEMUSEUM up to $300,000 in cash-flow support until October 31, 2024, paid in staged amounts and only when needed.
THEMUSEUM must provide monthly cash-flow projections, limit discretionary spending, honour community commitments and start a business-model review by June 1.

decisions.item: Ask the Region for matching support
decisions.detail: Council added a requirement that THEMUSEUM formally ask the Region of Waterloo, before July 1, to share half of the interim cost, or $150,000.
Council declined to postpone the final August 15 payment to the June 24 meeting, so the full amount stays available under the agreement.
Council granted an exemption from the Noise chapter of the Municipal Code for all downtown special events described in report CSD-2024-140.

debate: Delegates from THEMUSEUM said its operating model has been flawed for years, since it must earn about three-quarters of its revenue while most museums earn far less. They said cutting programming would reduce attendance, memberships and sponsorship, so the museum cannot cut its way to sustainability.

Several councillors questioned the short notice and asked why the Region had not been approached. They also asked how Council would hold THEMUSEUM to real change. One councillor asked about an interest-free loan. Delegates said a not-for-profit would struggle to repay it, and staff said repayment should not be assumed.

Supporters of deferring the final payment said it would let the Region weigh in and show Council was accountable to ratepayers. Opponents, including delegates and staff, said it would add weeks of uncertainty for staff and camp families. They also said it could undermine the board's decision to stay open.

Staff said a review and contingency plan would be hard to complete by the end of August, let alone by June 24. They said the museum's closure would likely hurt downtown foot traffic, businesses and parking revenue.

Many councillors said arts funding from the provincial and federal governments is inadequate. They said other partners, including the Region and the downtown business improvement area, should contribute, and some called for advocacy to senior governments.
